name: GATE CSE
fullName: Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering – Computer Science & Information Technology (CS)
conductingBody: IISc Bangalore and seven IITs on rotation for the National Coordination Board–GATE, Ministry of Education (GATE 2027: IIT Madras)
approxCandidates: ≈2.6 lakh registered and ≈2.1 lakh appeared for the CS paper in GATE 2026 (aggregator figures). GATE 2026 CS qualifying cut-off: 30 (General), 27 (OBC-NCL/EWS), 20 (SC/ST/PwD).
eligibility: Students in the 3rd year or higher of any UG programme, or graduates in engineering, technology, science, commerce or arts. No age limit. A candidate may take up to two papers from the allowed combinations.

notification.summary: GATE 2027 is being organised by IIT Madras. Registration on GOAPS opened in Aug/early Sep 2026 (reports differ). The regular-fee deadline was extended to 5 Oct 2026, and the late-fee window runs until 12 Oct 2026. The exams are scheduled on 6, 7, 13, 14, 20 and 21 Feb 2027, with results on 19 Mar 2027. DigiLocker-based verification is mandatory for Indian candidates. Dates come from news reports via web search; gate2027.iitm.ac.in could not be reached from the research sandbox.

importantDates.event: Exam days (CS slot to be announced)

notification.source: https://gate2027.iitm.ac.in (official), dates as reported by Careers360 (engineering.careers360.com/articles/gate-exam-dates) and CareerIndia

pattern.notes: Real paper: 65 questions for 100 marks. General Aptitude has 5 one-mark and 5 two-mark questions (15 marks). The CS section has 55 questions (85 marks), of which roughly 13 marks are Engineering Mathematics. Question types are MCQ, MSQ (multiple select) and NAT (numerical answer). Only MCQs carry negative marking: −1/3 for a 1-mark MCQ and −2/3 for a 2-mark MCQ. The 'marking' field above shows the 1-mark MCQ case, and 2-mark MCQs score +2 / −0.67. As instructed, this mock is MCQ-only: about 45–50% of the real CS paper consists of MSQ/NAT items, and these have been recast as single-answer MCQs. The question bank holds 60 original questions (10 GA + 50 CS). Since 2024 the CS paper has been held in two sessions (CS1/CS2), with scores normalised.

trendAnalysis.summary: This analysis covers GATE 2024 (IISc), 2025 (IIT Roorkee) and 2026 (IIT Guwahati) CS papers, each in two sessions. Difficulty is moderate to tough and calculation-heavy, with the CS1 and CS2 sets sometimes differing noticeably in difficulty. MSQ and NAT questions now make up close to half the paper, which makes guessing less effective. Programming & Data Structures (C code tracing, pointers, recursion, trees, hashing), Discrete Mathematics, OS, COA (caches, pipelining) and Theory of Computation remain the highest-weighted areas. Probability and Linear Algebra have grown at the expense of Calculus. General Aptitude (15 marks) is easy to moderate and highly scoring. The GATE 2026 CS qualifying cut-off was 30/100 (General).

pyqBlueprint.method: Compiled from the officially released GATE CS question papers and final answer keys (GATE 2024 IISc, 2025 IIT Roorkee, 2026 IIT Guwahati; both CS sessions where applicable) as summarised in public subject-wise analyses (MADE EASY, PW, Careers360, CollegeDunia), which web search confirmed for weightage (GA ≈ 15%, Engineering Maths ≈ 13%, with PDS, COA, OS, TOC and CN the heaviest core subjects; significant MSQ/NAT share). Full papers could not be fetched, so recurring concept + format + trap patterns were written from the drafter's own knowledge of these papers. NAT/MSQ archetypes are represented by their underlying computation recast as single-answer MCQs.

archetypes.pattern: Word meaning: synonym/antonym or the word that best fits a context
Grammar fill-in-the-blank: subject–verb agreement, prepositions, tense
Analogy between word pairs (tool : user, part : whole)
Short passage — which statement can be logically inferred (contrapositive traps)
Arithmetic word problems: work–time, mixtures, profit/discount, percentages
Probability with dice, coins or cards
Number properties: remainders, unit digits, divisibility
Data interpretation from a small table/chart: percentage change computations
Syllogism / logical deduction — which conclusion necessarily follows
Clock angles, calendars, ordering/seating arrangements
Painted cube cut into unit cubes; counting faces; paper folding/rotation of figures
Counting relations/functions with properties (reflexive, symmetric, onto) on finite sets
Propositional and first-order logic: tautologies, equivalences, negation of quantified statements
Graph theory: chromatic number, degrees/edges, connectivity bounds, matchings
Combinatorics: stars and bars, linear recurrences, pigeonhole
Group theory (order of elements, generators of cyclic groups), posets and lattices
Eigenvalues/eigenvectors and determinants of matrix functions
Rank and consistency of linear systems; number of solutions
Limits, maxima/minima and definite integrals of standard functions
Combinatorial probability (draws, dice, max/min of rolls)
Expectation and variance of standard distributions (uniform, Poisson, binomial, exponential)
K-map minimisation of a Boolean function given as minterms
Number representation: two’s complement ranges/overflow, IEEE-754 encoding, base conversion
Combinational/sequential circuits: MUX/decoder implementation, counters and timing
Cache mapping: tag/index/offset bits, set number for a block (direct/set-associative)
Pipelining: cycles for n instructions, speedup with unequal stage delays, stalls
Average memory access time for hierarchical/simultaneous access
Instruction formats and addressing modes; field widths
Trace a recursive C function and report its return value
C pointers, arrays, static/automatic storage — predict the printed output
Trees and heaps: BST traversals, heap array after insertions, tree counts
Stacks/queues: infix–postfix conversion and evaluation
Hashing with linear/quadratic probing or chaining — final slot positions
Solve divide-and-conquer recurrences (master theorem)
Properties of sorting algorithms (stability, in-place, worst case)
Graph algorithms on a small weighted graph: MST weight, Dijkstra distances, BFS/DFS order
Time complexity of nested loops with non-unit increments
Dynamic programming: LCS length, 0/1 knapsack value, matrix-chain cost
Minimum number of DFA states for a described language (suffix, nth-from-end, modulo counting)
Classify languages as regular / CFL / non-CFL
Decidability of problems about TMs/CFGs/regular languages
Regular expression for a described language and equivalence of expressions
FIRST/FOLLOW sets and LL(1)/LR parsing table entries
Compiler phases and lexical analysis: which phase detects an error, token counts
Intermediate code: basic blocks/leaders, control flow graphs, liveness
CPU scheduling (SRTF, RR, priority): average waiting/turnaround time
Page replacement (FIFO, LRU, optimal): number of faults; Belady’s anomaly
Semaphores and synchronisation: final values, possible outputs of concurrent code
Deadlock avoidance: minimum resources to guarantee no deadlock, Banker’s algorithm
Paging: page-table size, TLB effective access time, multi-level paging
Highest normal form of a relation from its FDs
Attribute closure and number of candidate keys
Output of an SQL query (GROUP BY/HAVING, nested queries) on a small table
Conflict/view serializability and recoverability of schedules
IPv4 subnetting/CIDR: hosts per subnet, same-subnet checks, number of subnets
Sliding-window protocols: maximum window sizes for GBN/SR, sequence-number bits
Link utilisation/throughput for stop-and-wait or windowed transmission with propagation delay
TCP congestion control (slow start, threshold), flow control and transport-layer behaviour

resources.notes: Each organising institute publishes the previous years' question papers and final answer keys on its GATE website (look for 'Previous Question Papers'), along with an official mock test link on the TCS iON interface. Candidates' response sheets and provisional keys are released after the exam. GATE 2024–26 papers were posted by IISc, IIT Roorkee and IIT Guwahati respectively.

questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to EPHEMERAL.
questions.explanation: Ephemeral means lasting for a very short time.

questions.question: Choose the correct option to fill the blank: "Neither the manager nor the employees ______ aware of the revised policy."
questions.explanation: With 'neither … nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Employees' is plural and the sentence is in the past, so 'were' is correct.

questions.question: Pen : Writer :: Scalpel : ?
questions.explanation: A pen is the primary tool of a writer, and a scalpel is the primary tool of a surgeon.

questions.question: A can complete a job in 12 days and B in 18 days. They work together for 4 days, after which A leaves. In how many more days will B finish the remaining work?
questions.explanation: Together they do 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36 per day, so in 4 days they do 20/36 = 5/9. The remaining 4/9 takes B (4/9) × 18 = 8 days.

questions.question: Two fair six-sided dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers is a prime number?
questions.explanation: The prime sums are 2 (1 way), 3 (2), 5 (4), 7 (6) and 11 (2), giving 15 favourable outcomes. 15/36 = 5/12.

questions.question: A 60-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 2 : 1. How many litres of water must be added to make the ratio 1 : 1?
questions.explanation: The mixture has milk = 40 L and water = 20 L. For a 1 : 1 ratio, water must equal 40 L, so add 20 L.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 2¹⁰⁰ is divided by 7?

Statements: Some cats are dogs. No dog is a rat.
Which of the following conclusions definitely follows?
questions.explanation: The cats that are dogs cannot be rats, so 'some cats are not rats' must be true. The other cats may or may not be rats, so the remaining options do not necessarily follow.

questions.question: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 3:40?
A solid cube painted on all six faces is cut into 64 identical smaller cubes. How many of the small cubes have exactly two painted faces?
questions.explanation: With 4 cubes per edge, each of the 12 edges has 4 − 2 = 2 cubes with exactly two painted faces. 12 × 2 = 24.

questions.question: How many binary relations on a set of 3 elements are both reflexive and symmetric?
questions.explanation: Reflexivity fixes all 3 diagonal pairs. Symmetry pairs up the 6 off-diagonal entries into 3 unordered pairs, each of which is either in or out, giving 2³ = 8.

questions.question: Which of the following propositional formulas is a tautology?
questions.explanation: If p → q is false, then p = T and q = F, which makes q → p true. So the disjunction is always true. The others fail: (p → q) → p is false at p = F; (p ∨ q) → (p ∧ q) and the biconditional are false at p = T, q = F.

questions.question: What is the chromatic number of a cycle graph with 7 vertices (C₇)?
questions.explanation: A cycle of odd length is not bipartite, so it needs 3 colours, and 3 colours always suffice for a cycle.

questions.question: In how many ways can 10 identical balls be placed in 4 distinct boxes so that no box is empty?
questions.explanation: By stars and bars, the number of positive integer solutions of x₁ + x₂ + x₃ + x₄ = 10 is C(9, 3) = 84.

questions.question: How many generators does a cyclic group of order 12 have?
questions.explanation: A cyclic group of order n has φ(n) generators, and φ(12) = 4 (the elements 1, 5, 7, 11 in ℤ₁₂).

questions.question: A 3 × 3 real matrix A has eigenvalues 1, 2 and 3. What is det(A² + I)?
questions.explanation: The eigenvalues of A² + I are λ² + 1, which are 2, 5 and 10. The determinant is their product: 2 × 5 × 10 = 100.

questions.question: What is the rank of the matrix [[1, 2, 3], [2, 4, 6], [1, 1, 1]]?
questions.explanation: Row 2 = 2 × Row 1. Rows 1 and 3 are linearly independent, so the rank is 2.

questions.question: What is the value of lim (x → 0) of (1 − cos x) / x²?
questions.explanation: 1 − cos x = 2 sin²(x/2), so the ratio is (1/2) × [sin(x/2)/(x/2)]², which tends to 1/2.

questions.question: A box contains 4 red and 6 blue balls. Two balls are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that both are of the same colour?
A random variable X is uniformly distributed on the interval [0, 6]. What is Var(X)?
What is the minimal sum-of-products form of F(A, B, C) = Σm(0, 2, 4, 5, 6), where A is the most significant bit?
questions.explanation: Minterms 0, 2, 4, 6 (all with C = 0) group to C′. Minterms 4 and 5 (A = 1, B = 0) group to AB′. So F = C′ + AB′.

questions.question: What is the range of integers that can be represented in 8-bit two's complement?
questions.explanation: An n-bit two's complement number ranges from −2ⁿ⁻¹ to 2ⁿ⁻¹ − 1, which for n = 8 is −128 to 127.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of 2-to-1 multiplexers needed to build a 16-to-1 multiplexer?
questions.explanation: A tree of 2:1 muxes uses 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 15. In general, an n:1 mux needs n − 1 two-to-one muxes.

questions.question: A byte-addressable machine with 32-bit addresses has a 32 KB direct-mapped cache with 64-byte blocks. How many bits are in the tag field?
questions.explanation: Offset = log₂64 = 6 bits. Lines = 32 KB / 64 B = 512, so index = 9 bits. Tag = 32 − 9 − 6 = 17 bits.

questions.question: A 5-stage pipeline in which every stage takes one clock cycle executes 100 independent instructions with no stalls. How many clock cycles are needed?
A cache has a hit time of 1 ns, a miss rate of 5% and a miss penalty of 100 ns. What is the average memory access time?
questions.explanation: AMAT = hit time + miss rate × miss penalty = 1 + 0.05 × 100 = 6 ns.

questions.question: In which addressing mode is the operand value itself contained in the instruction?
questions.explanation: In immediate addressing, the instruction carries the constant operand directly, for example ADD R1, #5.

questions.question: A 4-way set-associative cache of 64 KB uses 32-byte blocks. How many sets does the cache have?
questions.explanation: Number of lines = 64 KB / 32 B = 2048. Sets = 2048 / 4 = 512.
p points to a[1]. *(p + 2) = a[3] = 40 and p[-1] = a[0] = 10, so the sum is 50.
The static variable c keeps its value between calls, so g returns 2, 4 and 6. s = 12.

questions.question: The keys 50, 30, 70, 20, 40, 60, 80, 35 are inserted in that order into an initially empty binary search tree. What is the post-order traversal of the resulting tree?
What is the value of the postfix expression 6 2 3 + − 3 8 2 / + * ?
Keys 12, 22, 32, 15, 25 are inserted in that order into an empty hash table of size 10 with h(k) = k mod 10 and linear probing. At which index is 25 stored?
questions.explanation: 12 → 2, 22 → 3 (after collision), 32 → 4, 15 → 5. Then 25 hashes to 5, which is occupied, so it goes to 6.

questions.question: What is the asymptotic solution of the recurrence T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n log n?
questions.explanation: Here n^(log₂2) = n and f(n) = n log n = Θ(n log¹ n). By the extended case 2 of the master theorem, T(n) = Θ(n log² n).

questions.question: Which sorting algorithm has a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n) and sorts in place with O(1) extra space?
questions.explanation: Heap sort is O(n log n) in the worst case and in-place. Merge sort needs O(n) extra space, quick sort is O(n²) in the worst case, and insertion sort is O(n²).

questions.question: An undirected graph on vertices A, B, C, D has edge weights AB = 1, AC = 4, AD = 3, BC = 2, BD = 5, CD = 6. What is the weight of its minimum spanning tree?
questions.explanation: Kruskal's algorithm picks AB (1), then BC (2), then AD (3), which connects all four vertices. Total = 6.
The inner loop runs i times for i = 1, 2, 4, …, < n. The total is a geometric sum below 2n, so the complexity is Θ(n).

questions.question: What is the length of the longest common subsequence of the strings BACDBA and ABCBDA?
questions.explanation: One LCS is 'ACBA' (B-A-C-D-B-A against A-B-C-B-D-A). Dynamic programming confirms that the maximum length is 4.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of states in a DFA over {a, b} that accepts exactly the strings in which the number of a's is divisible by 3?
questions.explanation: The DFA only needs to track the count of a's mod 3, so it needs three states (remainders 0, 1, 2).

questions.question: Which of the following languages is NOT context-free?
questions.explanation: aⁿbⁿcⁿ requires matching three counts, which the pumping lemma for CFLs shows is impossible. The others can be generated by CFGs or recognised by PDAs.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of states in a DFA over {0, 1} that accepts all strings whose third symbol from the right end is 1?
questions.explanation: The DFA must remember the last 3 symbols, and all 2³ = 8 such suffixes are pairwise distinguishable. So 8 states are needed.

questions.question: Which of the following problems is undecidable?
options: Whether a given string belongs to the language of a given CFG
Whether a given CFG generates the empty language
Whether a given Turing machine halts on the blank tape
Whether a given DFA accepts at least one string
questions.explanation: The blank-tape halting problem reduces from the halting problem and is undecidable. DFA non-emptiness, CFG emptiness and CFG membership (CYK) are all decidable.

questions.question: Which regular expression denotes the set of all strings over {a, b} that do NOT contain 'aa' as a substring?
questions.explanation: Every a except possibly the last symbol must be followed by b, so the string splits into blocks of 'b' and 'ab' plus an optional final 'a'. (b + ab)* misses strings ending in a, (b + ba)* misses strings starting with a, and (b + ab)*a* allows 'aa'.

questions.question: For the grammar S → AB, A → aA | ε, B → b | ε (with $ as the end marker), what is FOLLOW(A)?
questions.explanation: From S → AB, FOLLOW(A) contains FIRST(B) − {ε} = {b}. Since B can derive ε, it also contains FOLLOW(S) = {$}. So FOLLOW(A) = {b, $}.

questions.question: In which phase of a compiler is an error such as adding an integer to a function name (a type mismatch) detected?
questions.explanation: Type checking is performed during semantic analysis, using the symbol table and the syntax tree.

questions.question: How many tokens does a C lexical analyser produce for the statement: int x = a1 + 25;
questions.explanation: The tokens are int, x, =, a1, +, 25 and ; which makes 7.

questions.question: Four processes arrive as follows (arrival time, CPU burst in ms): P1 (0, 7), P2 (1, 3), P3 (2, 8), P4 (4, 2). Under preemptive Shortest Remaining Time First scheduling, what is the average waiting time?
questions.explanation: The schedule is P1 0–1, P2 1–4, P4 4–6, P1 6–12, P3 12–20. Waiting times (completion − arrival − burst) are P1 = 5, P2 = 0, P3 = 10, P4 = 0. Average = 15/4 = 3.75 ms.

questions.question: With 3 initially empty frames and LRU page replacement, how many page faults occur for the reference string 2, 3, 2, 1, 5, 2, 4, 5, 3, 2, 5, 2?
questions.explanation: The faults occur at 2, 3, 1, 5 (evicts 3), 4 (evicts 1), 3 (evicts 2) and 2 (evicts 4). That makes 7 faults; the other references are hits.

questions.question: A counting semaphore is initialised to 10. Then 6 wait (P) operations and 4 signal (V) operations are performed on it. What is its final value?
questions.explanation: 10 − 6 + 4 = 8. The value never goes negative, so no process blocks.

questions.question: Three processes share a resource type, and each may need up to 4 instances. What is the minimum number of instances that guarantees the system can never deadlock?
questions.explanation: The worst case is that each process holds 3 instances (9 in total) while waiting for one more. One extra instance breaks the deadlock: 3 × (4 − 1) + 1 = 10.

questions.question: A system uses 32-bit logical addresses, 4 KB pages and 4-byte page-table entries, with a single-level page table. What is the size of the page table per process?
questions.explanation: Number of pages = 2³² / 2¹² = 2²⁰. Size = 2²⁰ × 4 B = 4 MB.

questions.question: Relation R(A, B, C, D) has the functional dependencies A → B, B → C, C → D. What is the highest normal form that R satisfies?
questions.explanation: The only candidate key is A. Because the key is a single attribute, there are no partial dependencies, so R is in 2NF. B → C and C → D are transitive dependencies of non-prime attributes, so R is not in 3NF.

questions.question: Relation R(A, B, C, D, E) has the functional dependencies AB → C, C → D, D → E, E → A. How many candidate keys does R have?
questions.explanation: B appears on no right-hand side, so it is in every key. AB⁺, BC⁺, BD⁺ and BE⁺ each equal ABCDE (for example BE: E → A, then AB → C → D). B alone is not a key, so the candidate keys are AB, BC, BD and BE.

questions.question:
Table Emp(eid, dept, salary) contains the rows (1, A, 50), (2, A, 60), (3, B, 70), (4, B, 40), (5, B, 30), (6, C, 90). How many rows does this query return?

SELECT dept, AVG(salary) FROM Emp
GROUP BY dept
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 AND AVG(salary) > 45;
questions.explanation: Dept A: count 2, average 55 → kept. Dept B: count 3, average 46.67 → kept. Dept C: count 1 → removed. So 2 rows are returned.

questions.question: Consider the schedule S: r1(X), r2(X), w1(X), w2(X). Which statement is true?
options: S is conflict serializable and equivalent to T1 → T2
S is conflict serializable and equivalent to T2 → T1
questions.explanation: r1(X) before w2(X) gives the edge T1 → T2, and r2(X) before w1(X) gives the edge T2 → T1. The precedence graph has a cycle, so S is not conflict serializable.

questions.question: How many usable host addresses does each subnet of 192.168.10.0/26 have?
questions.explanation: A /26 leaves 6 host bits: 2⁶ − 2 = 62 usable addresses (excluding the network and broadcast addresses).

questions.question: Which of the following IP addresses is in the same subnet as 172.16.45.14/20?
questions.explanation: A /20 mask is 255.255.240.0, so the third octet comes in blocks of 16. 45 lies in 32–47, giving the subnet 172.16.32.0 – 172.16.47.255. Only 172.16.47.200 falls in it.

questions.question: In the Go-Back-N protocol with 3-bit sequence numbers, what is the maximum sender window size?
questions.explanation: For Go-Back-N the window is at most 2ⁿ − 1 = 7. Selective Repeat would allow 2ⁿ⁻¹ = 4.

questions.question: A 10 Mbps link has a one-way propagation delay of 20 ms. Stop-and-wait is used with 1000-byte frames, and acknowledgement transmission time is negligible. What is the approximate link utilisation?
questions.explanation: Tₜ = 8000 bits / 10⁷ bps = 0.8 ms. Utilisation = Tₜ / (Tₜ + 2Tₚ) = 0.8 / (0.8 + 40) ≈ 1.96%.

questions.question: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to FRUGAL.
questions.explanation: Frugal means sparing or economical with money; its opposite is extravagant. Thrifty, economical and prudent are near-synonyms.

questions.question: Choose the correct option to fill the blank: “He insisted ______ paying the entire bill himself.”
questions.explanation: “Insist” takes the preposition “on” before a gerund: insisted on paying.

questions.question: “Everyone who completed the training received a certificate. Ravi did not receive a certificate.” Which of the following can be logically inferred?
options: Ravi did not attend the training.
Only those who completed the training received a certificate.
Ravi did not complete the training.
Ravi failed the final assessment of the training.
questions.explanation: Completed → certificate; its contrapositive is no certificate → not completed. Nothing is said about attendance, assessments or whether others got certificates.

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks his goods 40% above the cost price and then allows a discount of 20% on the marked price. His profit percentage is
questions.explanation: Selling price = 1.4 × 0.8 = 1.12 times the cost, i.e. a 12% profit. (20% simply subtracts the percentages.)

questions.question: Three fair coins are tossed together. The probability of getting at least two heads is
questions.explanation: Exactly two heads: 3 outcomes; three heads: 1 outcome. (3 + 1)/8 = 1/2.

questions.question: What is the units digit of 7²⁰²⁶?
questions.explanation: Units digits of powers of 7 cycle 7, 9, 3, 1 with period 4. 2026 = 4 × 506 + 2, so the units digit is 9.

questions.question: A company’s revenue was ₹200 crore in 2023 and ₹250 crore in 2024. Its profit was 10% of revenue in 2023 and 12% of revenue in 2024. By what percentage did the profit increase from 2023 to 2024?
questions.explanation: Profit: 0.10 × 200 = ₹20 crore and 0.12 × 250 = ₹30 crore. Increase = 10/20 = 50%.

questions.question:
Statements: All pens are books. Some books are bags.
Conclusions: I. Some pens are bags. II. Some bags are books.
Which conclusion(s) logically follow?
questions.explanation: “Some books are bags” converts to “some bags are books”, so II follows. The books that are bags need not be pens, so I does not necessarily follow.

questions.question: If 1 January 2025 was a Wednesday, what day of the week was 1 January 2026?
questions.explanation: 2025 is not a leap year, so it has 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 day. The day advances by one: Thursday.

questions.question: A cube is painted red on two opposite faces and blue on the remaining four faces. It is then cut into 27 identical smaller cubes. How many small cubes have exactly one red face and exactly one blue face (and no other painted face)?
questions.explanation: Such cubes lie on the edges where a red face meets a blue face, excluding corners. Each red face has 4 such edges with 1 middle cube each: 2 × 4 = 8. Corner cubes have three painted faces.

questions.question: Which of the following is logically equivalent to ¬∀x (P(x) → Q(x))?
What is the maximum number of edges in a simple undirected graph with 10 vertices that is disconnected?
questions.explanation: Make one isolated vertex and a complete graph K₉ on the rest: C(9, 2) = 36 edges. Any more edges would force connectivity.

questions.question: The sequence aₙ satisfies aₙ = 5aₙ₋₁ − 6aₙ₋₂ for n ≥ 2, with a₀ = 1 and a₁ = 4. What is a₃?
How many elements of order 4 are there in the cyclic group (Z₁₂, +)?
questions.explanation: A cyclic group of order 12 has φ(4) = 2 elements of order 4: 3 and 9.

questions.question: How many symmetric binary relations are there on a set with 4 elements?
questions.explanation: Each of the 4 diagonal pairs is free (2⁴) and each of the C(4,2) = 6 unordered off-diagonal pairs is included in both directions or not (2⁶): 2¹⁰ = 1024.

questions.question: What are the eigenvalues of the matrix [[4, 1], [2, 3]] (rows)?
questions.explanation: Characteristic equation λ² − 7λ + (12 − 2) = λ² − 7λ + 10 = 0 ⇒ λ = 2, 5 (sum 7 = trace, product 10 = determinant).

questions.question: The system x + y + z = 1, x + 2y + 3z = 2, 2x + 3y + 4z = 3 has
questions.explanation: The third equation is the sum of the first two, so the coefficient and augmented matrices both have rank 2 < 3 unknowns: the system is consistent with infinitely many solutions.

questions.question: What is the maximum value of f(x) = x e⁻ˣ for x ≥ 0?
questions.explanation: f′(x) = e⁻ˣ(1 − x) = 0 at x = 1, where f changes from increasing to decreasing. f(1) = 1/e.

questions.question: A fair six-sided die is rolled twice. What is the probability that the larger of the two numbers is 6?
X is a Poisson random variable with mean 2. What is E[X²]?
questions.explanation: For Poisson, Var(X) = mean = 2. E[X²] = Var(X) + (E[X])² = 2 + 4 = 6.

questions.question: What is the minimal sum-of-products form of F(A, B, C) = Σm(0, 2, 5, 7), where A is the most significant bit?
questions.explanation: m0 and m2 (A = 0, C = 0) group as A′C′; m5 and m7 (A = 1, C = 1) group as AC. F = A′C′ + AC (A XNOR C). A′C + AC′ is its complement.

questions.question: The 32-bit pattern 0x40A00000 is interpreted as an IEEE-754 single-precision number. Its value is
A 4-bit ripple counter is built from flip-flops each having a propagation delay of 10 ns. Ignoring other delays, the maximum clock frequency for reliable operation is
questions.explanation: In a ripple counter the delays add: 4 × 10 = 40 ns must elapse before the next clock edge. f_max = 1/40 ns = 25 MHz. (100 MHz would be the synchronous-counter value.)

questions.question: A byte-addressable machine has 24-bit physical addresses and a 16 KB direct-mapped cache with 32-byte blocks. How many bits are in the tag field?
questions.explanation: Offset = log₂32 = 5 bits; lines = 16 KB/32 B = 512 ⇒ index = 9 bits. Tag = 24 − 9 − 5 = 10 bits.

questions.question: A non-pipelined processor takes 50 ns per instruction. It is redesigned as a 5-stage pipeline with stage delays 10, 12, 8, 15 and 10 ns and a latch delay of 1 ns between stages. What is the speedup for a very large number of instructions (no stalls)?
questions.explanation: The pipeline clock is set by the slowest stage plus latch: 15 + 1 = 16 ns. Speedup ≈ 50/16 = 3.125. (3.33 ignores the latch delay.)

questions.question: A system has an L1 cache with hit time 2 ns and hit ratio 90%, backed by main memory with access time 100 ns. The cache is checked first, and on a miss main memory is accessed. What is the average memory access time?
questions.explanation: Hierarchical access: AMAT = 2 + 0.1 × 100 = 12 ns. (11.8 ns would apply if cache and memory were accessed simultaneously.)

questions.question: A processor has 32-bit instructions, an 8-bit opcode and 32 general-purpose registers. An instruction format holds the opcode, two register operands and an immediate field that uses all remaining bits. How wide is the immediate field?
questions.explanation: Each register specifier needs log₂32 = 5 bits. Immediate = 32 − 8 − 5 − 5 = 14 bits.

questions.question: A 4-way set-associative cache has 256 blocks in total. Main memory block number 1000 maps to which set (sets numbered from 0)?
questions.explanation: Number of sets = 256/4 = 64. Set = 1000 mod 64 = 1000 − 960 = 40. (232 = 1000 mod 256 is the direct-mapped line.)
f computes the sum of decimal digits: 2 + 0 + 2 + 6 = 10.
**q and *p both refer to x. **q = 10 sets x to 10; *p = *p + 1 makes it 11.
a is static: initialised once and retains its value (2, 3, 4). b is automatic: re-initialised to 1 each call, so it prints 2 every time.

questions.question: The keys 10, 20, 15, 30, 40 are inserted one by one into an initially empty binary max-heap stored in an array. What is the array after all insertions?
What is the postfix form of the infix expression a + b * (c − d) / e?
questions.explanation: * and / have equal precedence and are left-associative, so the expression is a + ((b * (c − d)) / e). b * (c − d) → b c d − *; dividing by e → b c d − * e /; adding a → a b c d − * e / +.

questions.question: A hash table of size 7 uses quadratic probing h(k, i) = (k + i²) mod 7 for i = 0, 1, 2, … The keys 10, 17 and 24 are inserted in that order into the empty table. In which slot is 24 stored?
questions.explanation: 10 → slot 3. 17: 3 is taken, i = 1 gives 4. 24: 3 taken, 4 taken, i = 2 gives (24 + 4) mod 7 = 0.

questions.question: What is the solution of the recurrence T(n) = 4T(n/2) + n²?
questions.explanation: n^(log₂4) = n² equals f(n) = n², so the master theorem’s case 2 gives Θ(n² log n).

questions.question: Which of the following sorting algorithms is stable in its standard array implementation?
questions.explanation: Merge sort preserves the relative order of equal keys when the merge takes from the left half on ties. Standard quick sort, heap sort and selection sort can reorder equal keys.

questions.question: A directed graph has edges A→B (4), A→C (1), C→B (2), B→D (1) and C→D (5). What is the shortest-path distance from A to D found by Dijkstra’s algorithm?

questions.explanation: For each i the inner loop runs about n/i times. Σ n/i = n·Hₙ = Θ(n log n).

questions.question: A 0/1 knapsack of capacity 7 is to be filled from items with (weight, value) = (1, 1), (3, 4), (4, 5) and (5, 7). What is the maximum total value?
questions.explanation: Candidate subsets within capacity 7: (3,4)+(4,5) → weight 7, value 9; (1,1)+(5,7) → weight 6, value 8; (1,1)+(4,5) → value 6; (1,1)+(3,4) → value 5. Item (5,7) cannot be combined with (3,4) or (4,5). Maximum = 9.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of states in a DFA over {a, b} that accepts exactly the strings ending in ab?
questions.explanation: States track the longest suffix matching a prefix of ab: ε, a, ab (accepting). These three are pairwise distinguishable, so 3 states are needed and suffice.

questions.question: Which of the following languages is context-free but NOT regular?
questions.explanation: aⁿbⁿ needs one stack (CFL) but unbounded counting (not regular). aⁿbⁿcⁿ and a^(n²) are not context-free; (ab)* is regular.

questions.question: Which of the following problems is decidable?
options: Whether a given Turing machine halts on every input
Whether a given context-free grammar generates the empty language
Whether two given context-free grammars generate the same language
Whether a given context-free grammar is ambiguous
questions.explanation: Emptiness of a CFG is decidable by marking generating variables. Totality of TMs, CFG equivalence and CFG ambiguity are undecidable.

questions.question: Which regular expression denotes the set of all strings over {0, 1} containing an even number of 0s?
questions.explanation: (1*01*0)* produces blocks with exactly two 0s each, with 1s anywhere between; the trailing 1* allows ending in 1s. (00)*1* misses strings like 0101; the others describe different languages.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of states of a DFA that reads a binary number from the most significant bit and accepts it if and only if its value is divisible by 5?
questions.explanation: Track the remainder mod 5: reading bit b moves r to (2r + b) mod 5. The 5 remainder states are pairwise distinguishable, so 5 states are needed.

questions.question: For the grammar S → AB, A → a | ε, B → b | ε, what is FIRST(S)?
questions.explanation: FIRST(A) = {a, ε}; since A can vanish, FIRST(B) = {b, ε} is added; since both can vanish, ε ∈ FIRST(S).

questions.question:
How many basic blocks does the following three-address code contain?

1: i = 1
2: t1 = i * 4
3: if t1 > 20 goto 6
4: i = i + 1
5: goto 2
6: x = t1
questions.explanation: Leaders: 1 (first statement), 2 (jump target), 4 (follows a conditional jump), 6 (jump target). Blocks: {1}, {2, 3}, {4, 5}, {6}.

questions.question: Which phase of a compiler uses a context-free grammar to check that the token stream forms a valid program structure?
questions.explanation: The parser (syntax analyser) checks the token sequence against the CFG. Lexical analysis uses regular expressions; semantic analysis checks types and scopes.

questions.question: Processes P1 (arrival 0, burst 5), P2 (arrival 1, burst 3) and P3 (arrival 1, burst 1) are scheduled by Round Robin with time quantum 2. P2 enters the ready queue before P3, and newly arrived processes are queued before a preempted process. What is the average waiting time?
questions.explanation: Gantt: P1 0–2, P2 2–4, P3 4–5, P1 5–7, P2 7–8, P1 8–9. Completion: P1 9, P2 8, P3 5. Waiting = completion − arrival − burst: 4, 4, 3. Average = 11/3 ≈ 3.67.

questions.question: With 4 initially empty frames and FIFO page replacement, how many page faults occur for the reference string 1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5?
questions.explanation: Faults on 1, 2, 3, 4 (4); 1, 2 hit; then 5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 each fault (6) as FIFO evicts the oldest page each time. Total 10 (more than the 9 faults with 3 frames — Belady’s anomaly).
Only P1 can start (S = 1, T = 0). Each print by one process enables exactly one print by the other, forcing strict alternation 0, 1, 0, 1, …

questions.question: Five processes share instances of a single resource type, and each process may need at most 3 instances. What is the minimum number of instances that guarantees deadlock can never occur?
questions.explanation: Worst case: every process holds 2 instances and waits for one more (10 held). One extra instance lets some process finish: 5 × (3 − 1) + 1 = 11.

questions.question: A system uses a single-level page table and a TLB. TLB lookup takes 10 ns, a memory access takes 100 ns and the TLB hit ratio is 90%. What is the effective memory access time?
Relation R(A, B, C) has the functional dependencies AB → C and C → A. What is the highest normal form satisfied by R?
questions.explanation: Candidate keys are AB and BC, so every attribute is prime and R is in 3NF. C → A violates BCNF because C is not a superkey.

questions.question: Relation R(A, B, C, D, E) has the functional dependencies A → B, BC → D and D → E. How many candidate keys does R have?
questions.explanation: A and C appear on no right-hand side, so every key contains both. {A, C}⁺ = {A, B, C, D, E}, so AC is the only candidate key.

questions.question:
Table Orders(cust, amount) contains the rows (A, 100), (B, 200), (A, 300), (C, 50), (B, 100). How many rows are returned by:

SELECT cust FROM Orders GROUP BY cust HAVING SUM(amount) > 250;
questions.explanation: Group sums: A = 400, B = 300, C = 50. Two groups (A and B) exceed 250.

questions.question: Consider the schedule r1(A), w2(A), w1(A), c1, c2. Which statement is correct?
options: It is conflict serializable, equivalent to T1 followed by T2.
It is conflict serializable, equivalent to T2 followed by T1.
It is conflict serializable, equivalent to both serial orders.
questions.explanation: r1(A) before w2(A) gives the edge T1 → T2; w2(A) before w1(A) gives T2 → T1. The precedence graph has a cycle, so the schedule is not conflict serializable.

questions.question: An organisation has the block 200.10.20.0/24 and wants to divide it into equal-sized subnets, each supporting at least 50 hosts. What is the maximum number of subnets possible?
questions.explanation: 50 hosts need 6 host bits (2⁶ − 2 = 62 usable; 5 bits give only 30). That leaves 2 subnet bits: 2² = 4 subnets of /26.

questions.question: In the Selective Repeat protocol with 4-bit sequence numbers, what is the maximum sender window size?
questions.explanation: Selective Repeat requires window ≤ 2^(k−1) = 2³ = 8 so that old and new frames are not confused. (15 = 2⁴ − 1 is the Go-Back-N limit.)

questions.question: A 1 Mbps link has a one-way propagation delay of 10 ms. Frames are 1000 bytes long and acknowledgement transmission time is negligible. What is the minimum sender window size (in frames) needed to achieve 100% utilisation?
questions.explanation: Transmission time = 8000 bits/10⁶ bps = 8 ms. A cycle lasts 8 + 2 × 10 = 28 ms, during which 28/8 = 3.5 frame times elapse. The window must be at least ⌈3.5⌉ = 4 frames.

questions.question: A TCP connection starts in slow start with a congestion window of 1 MSS and a slow-start threshold of 16 MSS. Assuming no losses, after how many round-trip times does the congestion window first reach 16 MSS?
questions.explanation: In slow start the window doubles every RTT: 1 → 2 → 4 → 8 → 16 MSS, i.e. after 4 RTTs.
